indication_area: Gastroenterology (chronic idiopathic constipation, IBS-C, opioid-induced constipation)
revenue_scope: U.S. Amitiza net sales as reported by Takeda, which records all Amitiza sales. 2008Q3-2011Q1: Sucampo Pharmaceuticals' 8-K earnings releases print 'net sales of Amitiza ... as reported by Takeda' in USD millions; Sucampo's FY2009 10-K states 'All sales of Amitiza in the U.S. and Canada ... are made through Takeda. Amitiza is currently marketed only in the U.S.', so this is U.S. net sales. 2011Q2-2022Q1: Amitiza net sales as Takeda prints them: the 'United States' / 'U.S.' region column of the product-sales tables from FY2015, and for FY2011-FY2014 the Amitiza product line labelled 'U.S.' in the FY2011-FY2013 statements and communications and printed in the FY2013-FY2014 statements and data books under 'Global major products' sales'. Takeda's FY2015 data book splits FY2014 Amitiza into United States 31.9, Europe and Canada 0.0 and Total 32.0, so the FY2011-FY2014 product line exceeds the U.S. column by at most 0.1 bn JPY. From FY2013 the sales amount includes royalty income, and from FY2014 royalty and service income, per the table notes; from FY2019 Takeda states the same.
geography: United States (2008Q3-2011Q1 rows are Takeda's Amitiza net sales as reported by Sucampo, marketed only in the U.S.; FY2011-FY2014 Takeda rows are the Amitiza product line, which Takeda's FY2015 data book shows as U.S. 31.9 of a 32.0 total for FY2014)

approval_evidence.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Amitiza (Lubiprostone Capsules) for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation in the adult population. ... It is approved, effective on the date of this letter (NDA 21-908, signed 1/31/2006).

series_start_reason: 2008Q3 is the earliest quarter for which any document prints Amitiza net sales as a quarterly figure. Sucampo's Q3 2009 release gives the third quarter of 2008 as the prior-year comparison ($50.8 million), and its Q4 2009 release gives the fourth quarter of 2008 ($58.7 million) and the 2008 year ($193.4 million). Net sales for the first and second quarters of 2008 are not printed separately: the nine months of 2008 are $134.7 million (Sucampo Q3 2009 Form 10-Q), so the first half is a combined $83.9 million that cannot be split by quarter. Takeda took over as the source from 2011Q2 (its fiscal Q1 FY2011, in JPY, read from the FY2012 Q1 statements). Amitiza launched in the U.S. in April 2006 (2006Q2), earlier than the first row. Takeda rows: 2011Q2 (Takeda fiscal Q1 FY2011) is the earliest quarter the published Takeda documents support. Takeda's FY2012 documents print Amitiza for FY2008 onward as annual figures only, plus the April-June, first-half and April-December 2011 figures, so quarters can be differenced from FY2011 Q1; FY2008-FY2010 are annual figures with no interim cumulative figure, and no Takeda document for fiscal years before FY2012 is published on takeda.com. 2011Q2 comes from the prior-year column of the FY2012 Q1 statements; later quarters are read from the quarter's own statements where Takeda prints a three-month column (Q1 and Q3) and are differenced from cumulative figures otherwise (Q2 from first half less Q1, Q4 from full year less nine months). 2015Q2 onward are the original rows, unchanged.
series_end_reason: Takeda's quarterly financial report for FY2021 Q4 (April 2021-March 2022; qr2021_q4_qfr_en.pdf) prints AMITIZA (U.S. 0.5 billion JPY in the quarter), whereas the FY2022 Q1 report (qr2022_q1_qfr_en.pdf) and every later quarterly report contain no AMITIZA revenue line (pdftotext finds zero mentions of Amitiza in each, except the FY2026 Q1 report, qr2026_q1_qfr_en.pdf, which mentions AMITIZA only in notes on a provision for the AMITIZA antitrust litigation).
notes: The series changes issuer and currency at 2011Q2. 2008Q3-2011Q1 are Sucampo's USD millions of Amitiza net sales as reported by Takeda; 2011Q2-2022Q1 are Takeda's own JPY (value_reported in millions of JPY, source_unit billions). Each row carries its currency, and the gold builder converts to USD by quarter. Sucampo's prose figures overlap the Takeda period (second quarter 2011 $61.4 million, third quarter 2011 $57.6 million, first quarter 2012 $60.7 million, second quarter 2012 $65.0 million) and are not used there, so the series keeps Takeda's own reporting from 2011Q2. Sucampo's product royalty revenue line (and its 3.2% royalty expense) is a royalty-holder line of a different scope and is not used. Sucampo year checks: 2009 quarters 49.7+49.5+52.0+58.0 = 209.2 (printed 209.2); 2010 quarters 54.3+53.4+57.0+55.3 = 220.0 (printed 220.0); 2008 third plus fourth quarter 109.5 equals the 193.4 year less the 83.9 first half implied by the nine-month 134.7. 2008Q3, 2008Q4, 2009Q1 and 2009Q2 are prior-year comparatives because the quarter's own release prints only product royalty revenue. Original Takeda notes: Takeda commercializes Amitiza in the U.S. under the Sucampo (now Mallinckrodt) license; this series is Takeda's own U.S. sales. Mallinckrodt's (after its acquisition of Sucampo) 10-Q 'Net sales of Amitiza' lines are royalty revenue on sales to Takeda, a different scope, not used. U.S. region column in JPY billions; the FY2015-FY2018 Q3 data books also print a US$ quarterly table (Amitiza FY15 Q1-Q4 77, 79, 81, 70 million USD), not used so the series keeps one currency. FY2018 Q4 (2019Q1) is derived as full-year U.S. less the first three quarters, and FY2019 Q2 (2019Q3) as first half less Q1. Full-year checks: FY2015 quarters sum to 37.1 (printed 37.2); FY2016 sum 33.8 (printed 33.7); FY2017 33.7 (printed 33.7); FY2018 sum 32.9 (printed 32.9); FY2019 sum 27.8 (printed U.S. 27.8); FY2020 sum 20.8 (printed 20.8); FY2021 sum 5.8 (printed 5.8). Generic competition began in 2021 and sales fell from FY2020 Q4. No launch quarter is cited. Rows 2011Q2-2015Q1 (FY2011-FY2014) were added: FY2011 quarters sum to 18.7 (printed 18.7); FY2012 22.3 (printed 22.3); FY2013 25.6 (printed 25.7); FY2014 31.9 (printed 32.0), the last two differing by rounding of 0.1 bn JPY inputs. Second-quarter rows are first half less Q1; for FY2013 and FY2014 the three-term difference (nine months less Q1 less Q3) is 0.1 higher (6.0 and 7.4), which is rounding. Takeda labels these tables 'U.S.' in FY2011-FY2013 communications and statements and 'Global' in FY2013-FY2014 statements and data books; the FY2012 Q2 data book heads its table 'Sales of products outside Japan'. Takeda's regional split of Amitiza exists only from the FY2015 documents (FY2014 comparatives); the non-U.S. part there is 0.0-0.1 bn JPY.
search_log: Same Takeda document set as Dexilant: takeda.com quarterly-results pages FY2012-FY2020 (all PDFs) and the FY2020-FY2026 quarterly financial reports, read with pdftotext/pdfplumber.

FY2018 Q4 data book contains no Amitiza row; FY2018 Q4 derived from qr2018_q4_f_en.pdf (U.S. 32.9) and the Q3 data book (nine-month U.S. 25.8).

FY2022 Q1 report onward (qr2022_q1_qfr_en.pdf through qr2026_q1_qfr_en.pdf, 17 reports): no AMITIZA revenue line (FY2026 Q1 mentions AMITIZA only in notes on the antitrust-litigation provision), so Takeda stopped reporting the line after FY2021 Q4.

Scope: Sucampo FY2009 Form 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1365216/000095012310024764/c97731e10vk.htm): 'All sales of Amitiza in the U.S. and Canada, including those arranged by our specialty sales force, are made through Takeda. reviewed_anomalies.2011Q2: Read at source: the series changes issuer and currency here. 2011Q1 is Sucampo's USD 50.7 million and 2011Q2 is Takeda's JPY 5.0 billion (5,000 million), a step in raw value_reported that is a unit change, not a sales movement. Sucampo's own release for the same quarter prints USD 61.4 million for the second quarter 2011 (000115752311004735/a6820517ex99-1.htm), consistent with JPY 5.0 billion at an exchange rate near 80 yen per dollar. Kept as printed.
